title: DNA structure
examples: What are the three parts that make up a single nucleotide?
How does the pairing of the bases determine the structure?
Can you explain the difference between the sugar in DNA and RNA?

explain.say: Today we are learning about the amazing structure of DNA.
A nucleotide is the basic building block of DNA.
The four nitrogenous bases are adenine, thymine, guanine, and cytosine.
Base pairing rules are very important for DNA structure.

draw.text: A pairs with T; G pairs with C

explain.say: The two strands twist around each other to form a double helix.
In real life, DNA is what carries the instructions for life.

faq.q: What are the three parts of a nucleotide?
faq.a: A nucleotide is made of a phosphate group, a deoxyribose sugar, and a nitrogenous base.
asks: What makes up the building block of DNA?
Can you name the components of a nucleotide?

faq.q: Why do A and T always pair together?
faq.a: They pair specifically because of the number of hydrogen bonds they can form, which keeps the structure stable.
asks: What is the rule for base pairing?
Does the pairing depend on the base type?

faq.q: What is the difference between the two strands?
faq.a: The two strands run in opposite directions, which is called anti-parallel.

faq.q: What does the double helix shape represent?
faq.a: It shows that the two strands are wound around each other like a spiral staircase.
asks: What is the overall shape of DNA?
Why is it called a helix?

faq.q: Are the bases the same in DNA and RNA?
faq.a: No, DNA uses thymine, while RNA uses uracil instead of thymine.
asks: Is there a difference between DNA and RNA bases?
What base is in RNA instead of DNA?

facts: DNA is a polymer made of repeating nucleotide units.
Adenine always pairs with Thymine, and Guanine always pairs with Cytosine.
The structure is described as a double helix because of its spiral shape.
The sugar in DNA is deoxyribose.

quiz.say: Which pair of bases always forms three hydrogen bonds?
quiz.show: A) A-T, B) G-C, C) A-C
quiz.why: Guanine and Cytosine form three hydrogen bonds, making this pairing very stable.

wrong.0: This pair only forms two hydrogen bonds, which is less stable than G-C.
wrong.1: Adenine and Cytosine do not naturally pair together in the DNA structure.
wrong.2: Bases must pair with a complementary base, not with the same base.

quiz.say: If one strand has the sequence A-T-G, what is the complementary strand?
quiz.why: You must replace A with T, T with A, and G with C to find the complement.

wrong.0: You must change the G to C, not keep it as G.
wrong.2: This is the same sequence, not the complementary one.
wrong.3: This uses Uracil, which is found in RNA, not DNA.

quiz.say: The overall shape of the DNA molecule is best described as:
quiz.why: The structure twists into a recognizable spiral shape, like a ladder.

wrong.0: DNA is built from two separate, yet connected, strands.
wrong.2: The molecule does not remain straight; it coils around itself.
wrong.3: It has a distinct three-dimensional twist, not a flat appearance.
